Cycle Tracker records the first day of each period and uses the calendar method to estimate your menstrual cycle, predicting the next period, ovulation day, and ovulation window, and syncs the next period as a countdown event on the Home screen. All data is stored only on this device.

Tap any date on the calendar to add a daily log for that day (sex, bleeding and discharge, physical symptoms, mood, or your own entry). Daily logs are only a record and do not affect cycle or ovulation predictions, nor do they light up the period dot. Jotting down a symptom will not change the forecast.

· Menstrual: from day 1 of bleeding to its end, usually 3–7 days, shown as the dark segment on the ring.
· Follicular: after menstruation ends until before ovulation, follicles mature and the uterine lining rebuilds.
· Ovulation: ovulation day is generally about 14 days before the next period. The ~2 days on either side are the highest-fertility window.
· Luteal: after ovulation until the next period, the body secretes progesterone to maintain the lining. If no pregnancy, the lining sheds and the next menstrual phase begins.

· The background color of a date shows the phase it falls in.
· Filled dot: a logged period day.
· Hollow dot: a predicted period day, which becomes filled when it arrives.
· Small dot at top-right: there is a daily log that day. Tap the day to view it.
· Thin blue border: today, thick blue border: the currently selected date, which disappears when details are collapsed.

Cycle length and period duration vary from person to person. Mood, stress, sleep, travel, and illness can all shift the cycle earlier or later. The calendar method uses averages and may be off by several days from actual ovulation. Results are for reference only and are not a basis for contraception or medical diagnosis. If your cycle is long-term irregular or you feel unwell, please consult a doctor.

This feature uses the calendar method: the ovulation day is roughly the predicted first day of the next period minus 14 days. When periods are longer, the ovulation day and phase boundaries are auto-adjusted—the follicular phase is no shorter than 2 days and the luteal phase no shorter than 11 days, both within medically accepted ranges. Cycles fluctuate with stress, routine, illness, etc. Results are for reference only and are not a basis for contraception or medical diagnosis. If you have menstrual irregularities or health concerns, please consult a doctor.

Note: withdrawal is not an effective contraceptive method and the risk of pregnancy is high. If you used this method, please switch to \"Unprotected sex\", keep watching your body, and assess yourself promptly. It also does not prevent sexually transmitted infections.

Emergency contraception is most effective within 72 hours after sex — the sooner, the better. For ongoing birth control, ask a doctor about short-acting oral contraceptives (taken on a regular cycle). Please protect yourself, get checked if needed, and guard against sexually transmitted infections.
